properties.name: Corporate Core
properties.status: Materially comfortable corporate center under pervasive credentialing and surveillance
properties.known_for: Flagship offices, high-end public space, employment-linked housing, transit, nightlife, and overlapping corporate security
properties.access: Public pedestrian access with checkpoints, identity systems, traffic monitoring, and dense surveillance
properties.description: The Corporate Core is the clean, safe, materially comfortable Seattle that corporate employment can buy. There is no enclosing wall and pedestrians can enter; unfamiliarity alone does not trigger intervention. Control instead comes through checkpoints, identity systems, surveillance, traffic monitoring, credentialing, employment-linked housing, status pressure, and reciprocal security arrangements that make the district highly desirable while keeping daily life legible to institutions.
properties.governance: Seattle civic authority operates inside a dense web of reciprocal corporate-security and credentialing arrangements
properties.communities: Corporate employees, service workers, residents in employment-linked housing, visitors, commuters, and municipal staff
properties.organizations: Major megacorporations, corporate-security contractors, civic agencies, hospitality and transit operators
properties.connections: Puget Sound waterfront, Mercer transit links, I-5, Meridian, Queen Anne, and Old City

properties.name: Queen Anne
properties.status: Primary enclave of Seattle’s post-Resonance wealthy elite
properties.known_for: Large private compounds, elegant residences, private schools, elite clubs, fine dining, golf, yacht culture, charities, and discreet security
properties.access: Public roads remain open, but outsiders are conspicuous under overlapping private-security observation
properties.description: Queen Anne is Seattle’s primary enclave of post-Resonance wealth: manicured private compounds and roughly one-to-four-acre estates where geography permits, elegant apartments toward the south, private schools, clubs, fine dining, golf, yacht culture, charities, and elaborate social rituals. Public roads are open, but overlapping security systems make outsiders continuously visible. Vaelis Thorne, a powerful Drow socialite and elite hostess, is one of the district’s prominent social figures.
properties.governance: Seattle jurisdiction remains in force while estate associations, private institutions, and contracted security shape daily life
properties.communities: Wealthy families, executives, elite professionals, domestic and service workers, private-school communities, club members, and marina residents
properties.organizations: Private schools, elite clubs, charities, marina organizations, estate security networks, and Dominion subcontract security
properties.connections: Mercer and the Corporate Core to the south, Salmon Bay and Ballard Reach to the north, Puget Sound to the west, and Lake Union to the east

properties.name: Helios Corridor
properties.status: Helios-dominated corporate habitat and biomedical enclave
properties.known_for: Corporate housing, hospitals, biotech research, regenerative medicine, clinics, laboratories, and employee services
properties.access: Public-facing clinics and commercial facilities mixed with credentialed Helios residential, research, and logistics space
properties.description: Helios Corridor is a property-defined corporate habitat rather than a conventional neighborhood. Helios Biotech requires its employees to live within corporate buildings and folds work, housing, healthcare, transportation, food, recreation, professional development, social life, and security into one attractive and highly functional ecosystem. The surrounding corridor of hospitals, clinics, biotech startups, contract laboratories, suppliers, restaurants, training facilities, and corporate housing is either Helios-owned or economically dependent on it. Dr. Aurelia Vale is the public head of Helios Biotech.
properties.governance: Seattle retains technical jurisdiction, but Helios Biotech dominates property, services, security, and access and keeps municipal authorities at arm’s length
properties.communities: Helios employees and families, clinicians, researchers, contract-lab staff, biotech workers, suppliers, trainees, and service workers
properties.organizations: Helios Biotech, hospitals, specialty clinics, biotech startups, contract laboratories, medical suppliers, research contractors, and clinical logistics firms
properties.connections: Property enclaves along the west, south, and east shores of Lake Union, including structures on or over the water; no Helios district frontage on the north shore
properties.gm_notes: Dr. Aurelia Vale is Aurum Rex, the Dragon, one of the principal Cabal powers. Helios Biotech is connected to Project Chimera. These facts are GM-only and must not appear in player-facing data.

properties.name: Meridian
properties.status: Professional interface for Seattle's gray and black economies
properties.known_for: Lake Washington ferries, the Seam, salvage markets, fixers, and expedition outfitters
properties.access: I-5 on the west, Lake Washington on the east, and guarded ferry terminals
properties.governance: Nominal Seattle authority layered over market customs, broker networks, and venue-specific neutrality
properties.communities: Traders, runners, ferry crews, salvage brokers, information dealers, and expedition teams
properties.organizations: Madison Terminal, Leschi Terminal, Afterimage, and the Third Door
properties.connections: Corporate Core to Meridian to Lake Washington ferries to the Silicon Wilds; returning salvage moves toward Gasworks and corporate buyers
properties.description: Between I-5 and Lake Washington, from the ruined I-90 corridor north to ruined SR-520, Meridian is Seattle's principal staging and trading interface with the Silicon Wilds. Information is currency here: ferries, salvage markets, outfitters, fixers, and brokers move people, rumors, and recovered technology between the city and the Eastside frontier.
properties.gm_notes: Afterimage is not neutral ground. The Third Door is neutral runner ground overseen by Etta 'Switch' Mercer, Garran 'Rampart' Okoye, and Ilyra 'Copper' Venn. Admission mechanics remain unresolved canon.

properties.name: Old City
properties.status: Working-class district held together by practical continuity and benign neglect
properties.known_for: Genuine older Seattle buildings, multigenerational neighborhoods, inexpensive commerce, shelters, utility infrastructure, and pragmatic tolerance
properties.access: Open city streets with uneven municipal attention and few formal barriers
properties.description: Old City is the common street name for a broad swath of older Seattle that survived largely because nobody cared enough to remake it. Its buildings and streets are genuinely old rather than a recreated historic district. The defining attitude is practical continuity: residents tend to meet metahumans, awakened people, cybernetics, corporations, outsiders, and strange post-Resonance events with pragmatic indifference rather than ideology.
properties.governance: Seattle municipal government technically governs the district but exercises relatively little day-to-day influence
properties.communities: Retirees, service workers, merchants, clergy, artists, low-level corporate workers, unhoused residents, and newcomers
properties.connections: Yesler and the Corporate Core to the north, S Spokane to the south, the Duwamish Waterway to the west, and I-5 to the east
properties.gm_notes: The Adventure 1 underground settlement beneath Old City was relocated intact by a Prometheus Shard. Its destination remains unknown. Do not imply that abandoned tunnels necessarily contain treasure, contamination, a replacement settlement, or any other resolved explanation.

properties.name: Ballard Reach
properties.status: Maritime district balancing independence with practical mutual dependence
properties.known_for: Fishing, salvage, boat repair, small shipyards, floating structures, smuggling, markets, marine trades, and independent manufacturing
properties.access: Water routes, industrial roads, docks, floating walkways, and neighborhood streets
properties.description: Ballard Reach is defined by the sea, freedom, maritime competence, independence, and the practical mutual dependence required to survive on the water. Roughly half the district is conventional land neighborhoods and industrial waterfront and half is docks, floating structures, and water-based settlement. Persistent cultural friction with Queen Anne is most visible where mega-yacht culture meets Ballard boats, but there is no organized conflict at campaign start.
properties.governance: The informal Captains’ Council handles practical disputes and common concerns without formal elections or municipal-style statute
properties.communities: Fishing crews, salvagers, boatbuilders, marine mechanics, traders, smugglers, floating-house residents, and other maritime families
properties.organizations: Captains’ Council, independent boatyards, repair shops, markets, small shipyards, and marine trades
properties.connections: Salmon Bay separates Ballard Reach from Queen Anne; the eastern boundary with Gasworks is intentionally fuzzy around roughly 8th Avenue NW

properties.name: Gasworks
properties.known_for: Prototyping, fabrication, salvage engineering, art, and experimental technology
properties.access: North of the Lake Washington Ship Canal between roughly 8th Avenue NW and the Ship Canal Bridge
properties.governance: Major decisions move through committees, workshop consensus, custom, reputation, and technical credibility. Chief Engineer Imani Calder chairs the council and serves as the de facto public face, but is not a mayor or centralized executive.
properties.communities: Riggers, engineers, artists, inventors, salvage crews, apprentices, and small workshops
properties.organizations: Greater Seattle Workshop Exchange (Gasworks), the Foundry, neighborhood workshops, manufactories, and Eriador, Inc.
properties.connections: Meridian supplies Eastside salvage; Gasworks prototypes move to Forgetown for mass production
properties.description: Gasworks is a maker district built on productive anarchy. Small workshops, manufactories, and the Foundry turn salvage into practical machines, art, prototypes, and experimental technology. The Greater Seattle Workshop Exchange keeps technical exchange unusually open, while reputation, workshop custom, and committee consensus substitute for centralized government. Chief Engineer Imani Calder chairs the council and is the district’s most visible spokesperson.
properties.gm_notes: Rumors concerning structures or inhabitants beneath Gas Works Park remain unresolved. The Foundry will blacklist members who disguise purpose-built weapons as dual-use projects.
properties.events: AQRE/The Works is the district's annual exposition and induction festival.

properties.name: University Enclave
properties.status: Traditional university governed through the corporate UW Compact
properties.known_for: Corporate research domains, independent humanities, and two expended Prometheus Shards
properties.access: Public academic spaces; controlled laboratories and Dominion-secured perimeter zones
properties.governance: University administration and faculty governance constrained by the seven-party UW Compact
properties.communities: Students, faculty, researchers, corporate scholars, and underfunded independent humanities departments
properties.organizations: Dominion, Neuracore, Helion, OmniTrine, Verdant, AstraVail, and ChimeraGene
properties.connections: A major recruitment and research nexus linking Seattle's corporations, civic institutions, and technical labor market
properties.description: The University of Washington still retains recognizable academic governance, but seven corporations divide its most valuable research domains through the UW Compact. Public campus life continues beside controlled laboratories, corporate scholarship pipelines, and independent humanities departments that survive with little funding.
properties.gm_notes: The UW Compact negotiations helped create the Council, although only five of the seven Compact signatories later joined it. Adyton is not on campus and its location remains unknown. The KBDJ extraction details remain unresolved.

properties.name: The South End
properties.status: Ordinary municipal district sustained by neighborhood institutions
properties.known_for: Affordable housing, families, schools, churches, small businesses, and essential labor
properties.access: South of I-90 and east of I-5, with porous edges and unreliable infrastructure
properties.governance: Seattle municipal government without a single district ruler; practical authority is distributed among neighborhood and labor groups
properties.communities: Immigrant and metahuman families, municipal workers, tradespeople, congregations, and small businesses
properties.organizations: The Yardmen, Southline Union, and Porchlight Boys
properties.connections: Residential and labor communities link central Seattle to Bombshell and the southern approaches
properties.description: The South End is run-down but functioning: a broad working district where families, schools, churches, trades, and small businesses keep ordinary life going without Corporate Core investment. Its geographic and social boundary with Bombshell is porous rather than clean.

properties.name: Bombshell
properties.status: Inhabited war ruin with weak municipal services
properties.known_for: SoDo and Duwamish ruins, warehouses, rail yards, mutual aid, gangs, and Boeing Field
properties.access: Usable industrial corridors and neighborhood streets separated by exclusion blocks and damaged infrastructure
properties.governance: Fragmented municipal presence, neighborhood rebuilding groups, protection networks, gangs, and corporate intermediaries
properties.communities: Long-term residents, displaced families, industrial workers, scavengers, metahuman communities, and mutual-aid crews
properties.organizations: Bombshell Mutual Works, Church of the Shattered Glass, the Cinders, Copperheads, and Rail Dogs
properties.connections: Industrial and rail corridors connect the Corporate Core and South End to Boeing Field and Tacoma
properties.description: Bombshell spans the SoDo, Georgetown, Duwamish, and southeastern war zone. It is both ruin and inhabited district: functional warehouses, rail lines, homes, churches, and mutual-aid projects stand beside shattered exclusion blocks and the fortified Boeing Field complex.
properties.gm_notes: Auntie Lee Varga leads Bombshell Mutual Works. Sister Rhea Calder sincerely worships Abraxas through the Church of the Shattered Glass. Corporate exploitation generally operates through intermediaries.

properties.name: West Seattle
properties.status: Semi-autonomous Seattle district under a civic compact
properties.known_for: Neighborhood government, local defense, food resilience, controlled bridges, and ferries
properties.access: West Seattle High Bridge, 1st Avenue South Bridge, ferries, and guarded checkpoints
properties.governance: West Seattle Civic Compact led by the Compact Council and Council Steward Miriam 'Miri' Hale
properties.communities: Neighborhood associations, fishing and food cooperatives, families, bridge crews, and volunteer defenders
properties.organizations: Compact Council, Civic Guard, Town Square, Open Signal Coalition, and Vesper Syndicate
properties.connections: Surviving bridges and ferries connect the peninsula to central and southern Seattle; local fishing compacts support food security
properties.description: West Seattle remains formally part of Seattle but operates with unusual autonomy under the West Seattle Civic Compact. Controlled bridges, neighborhood government, the Civic Guard, ferry links, and local food systems make the peninsula resilient and politically distinct.
properties.gm_notes: Commander Tomas 'Tom' Reyes leads the Civic Guard. The Open Signal Coalition is publicly independent but covertly supported by Vesper Syndicate as part of its psychoactive neurofeed effort.
